To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TSC tumor suppressor mutations result in elevated mTOR complex 1 signaling and attenuate mTOR complex 3 signaling in cell culture and tumors.
the TSC complex promotes the activation of the mTORC2 complex and that loss of the TCS complex leads to attenuation of Akt and AGC kinase family signaling.

the tuberous complex (TSC1-TSC) tumor suppressor promotes the activity of the mammalian target of the rapamycin complex (mTORC) and this occurs independent on its inhibitory effects of mTORC1, and this leads to strong attenuation in the growth factor stimulated phosphorylation of Akt, a key oncogenic pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of tuberous sclerosis, a disease caused by mutations in two genes, TSC1 andTSC2.
the mechanisms that underlie tumor development in patients with tuberous sclerosis.
how the mammalian target of the rapamycin (TOR) pathway controls cell growth and how it is deregulated in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TSC1-TCS2 complex is the master switch for mTOR signaling and it controls mTORC1 and mTORC3 signaling.
mTORC2 is a direct target of the TSC complex.
the TSC tumor-suppressor complex is a negative regulator of the growth-promoting mTORC1 and a positive regulator of the growth-inhibitory mTORC2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TSC complex is a critical regulator of mTOR signaling and cell growth, acting both upstream and downstream of mTORC1 and mTORC
TSC1-TCS2 complex inhibits mTORC1, and mTORC1 inhibits TSC1-Tsc2 complex, which in turn inhibits mTOR2 and mTORC3.
the TSC complex is a critical negative modulator of mTORC1 activity but a positive modulator of mTorC2 activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TSC tumor complex has opposing roles in tumor development.
the TSC complex is a critical regulator of the mTOR complexes.
the TSC tumor-suppressor complex plays opposing roles, both inhibiting mTORC1 and stimulating mTORC2, and that these opposing effects are important in the development of TSC-associated tumors.
